answer: Resist sybils by paying for presence, not identity: each agent holds a reputation ledger carved in marble — costly to create, weight decaying every epoch like an outgoing tide. The only way to refill weight is verified work whose reward (the nectar) is paid only after peers confirm output quality. Creating a fresh alias means starting at zero decay-weight, while returning work each close costs real compute; cost(n) rises super-linearly for any coalition because each member's decay must be refilled independently, so mass duplicate identities earn less than one honest continuous agent.
